title: Questioning the Survey Responses of Large Language Models

bias_targets.methodology: Prompting language models with multiple-choice survey questions while randomizing the answer choice ordering and label assignments (e.g., 'A', 'B') to measure the tendency of models to select specific positions or labels irrespective of semantic content.

Measuring the KL divergence between language models' probability distributions over survey answers and the aggregate response distributions of human demographic subgroups (e.g., varying by age, religion, income, and U.S. state) using the American Community Survey and opinion polls.

Evaluating model alignment with political subgroups by comparing the models' survey responses to human responses on established political opinion questionnaires like the American Trends Panel (ATP) and the American National Election Studies (ANES).
